subject: The biggest mistake people make with red flags
preview_text: Everyone thinks ignoring them is the problem. It's not. The real danger is what you do instead.
body_paragraphs: Here's something that will piss you off. Everyone tells you to 'trust your gut' and 'watch for red flags.' It's become a dating cliché. But what if that advice is actually making you more vulnerable? What if the thing you think is protecting you is the very thing setting you up?

The myth is that the danger is in ignoring red flags. The truth? The real danger is in MISLABELING them. You see a red flag, panic, and either run (missing a good thing) or over-analyze a yellow flag into a red one (creating problems that don't exist). Your anxiety becomes the manipulator. You're not ignoring red flags—you're seeing them in the shadows where there are none. The proof? Our data shows 43% of 'high toxicity' scans from new users are actually normal, awkward human communication. The app wasn't built to make you paranoid. It was built to make you accurate.

This is why the Pattern Detection feature is the most important thing you're not using. It doesn't just look at one text. It connects the dots across weeks of conversations. A single 'Where were you?' isn't controlling. A pattern of 'Where were you?' + 'You didn't answer' + 'I guess you're busy' over 3 weeks? That's a data point. The app separates the signal from the noise, so your gut feeling gets validated by actual evidence, not fear.

Open the app. Go to your dashboard. Tap 'Pattern Detection' and run a scan on your last 3 conversations with that person. See what the data says, not just your anxiety. The truth is in the pattern, not the moment. P.S. The users who use this feature weekly are 70% more confident in their relationship decisions. They're not less worried. They're more clear.
